title: feat: add deterministic API model ordering
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Orders Official models by modality: text, image, video, 3D, audio, realtime, then embedding.
- Places each category’s configured default first, then stable models before alpha/preview models, with newest additions first and model ID as the final tie-break.
- Places Community models after Official models, ordered by registration date and then model ID; Community creation time is exposed through existing `added_date` metadata.
- Applies ordering once in the generation registry so `/models`, `/v1/models`, modality catalogs, visibility, permission, and balance filters preserve the same sequence.
- Keeps alias resolution tied to declaration order, independent of catalog presentation sorting.

Visible ordering changes: Community text models move from the second group to the end, and audio now appears before realtime.

Checks: `npx vitest run src/community-endpoints.test.ts`; `npx vitest run test/openapi-json.test.ts`; `npm run typecheck`; Biome on changed files.

gist.headline: The model shelf is sorted
gist.blurb: The model catalog got a careful bit of garden tending. Official blooms now appear by modality and maturity, while community creations gather together at the end instead of wandering through the text patch.
gist.summary: The generation registry now deterministically orders Official models by modality (text, image, video, 3D, audio, realtime, embedding), puts each modality default and stable/newer models first, and lists Community models afterward by registration date.
gist.impact: Users and API clients will see the same predictable model sequence across /models, /v1/models, modality catalogs, visibility, permission, and balance-filtered results, with audio now preceding realtime and Community text models grouped at the end.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy model-library garden: Polli acts as a meticulous librarian/gardener arranging labeled seed packets on shelves by modality, with Official flowers in clearly ordered rows and Community seedlings in a welcoming final bed. A CRT monitor robot can admire the tidy catalog while subtle signs show text, image, video, 3D, audio, realtime, and embedding symbols.
